t: You're looking at the National Windrush Monument, a bronze sculpture in Waterloo station. It commemorates the British African-Caribbean immigrants who arrived in the United Kingdom aboard HMT Empire Windrush in 1948, the first of what became known as the Windrush generation. The sculptor is Basil Watson, a Jamaican artist. Among the crowds of commuters passing through the station, the monument asks you to stop and remember those who came.
